competitors: Competitor A — AI copilot bundled with the incumbent productivity suite
Competitor B — standalone chat assistant sold per seat to enterprises
Build-your-own — open-weight model plus an internal chat front end
enterprise_ai_assistant.positioning: Gemini Enterprise is the agent platform for the whole company, not a sidebar in one productivity suite: it searches and acts across the systems employees already use (Workspace, Microsoft 365, CRM, ticketing, data warehouses), ships pre-built agents, and lets the organisation build and govern its own agents on Google Cloud with enterprise controls.
strengths: Grounded answers across many connected sources with permissions respected at query time
Agent building for business users (no-code) and developers (ADK, Agent Engine) on one governed platform
Security and compliance posture of Google Cloud: data not used to train models, customer-managed encryption options, data residency options (verify per region/edition)
Choice of Gemini model tiers to balance quality and cost per use case
Works for mixed estates — does not require moving everyone off the incumbent suite first
landmines: Ask: 'How many of your systems of record can the assistant search today, with each user's own permissions?'
Ask: 'Can business teams build and share their own agents, and who governs them centrally?'
Ask: 'What does the licence cost if only 30% of seats are heavy users — can you mix tiers?'
Ask: 'Where are prompts and responses stored, for how long, and can you prove they are not used for training?'
Ask: 'How do you evaluate answer quality before rolling out to 2,000 people?'

objections.objection: We already own the incumbent suite; its copilot is 'free' with our agreement.
objections.response: Check what is actually included versus add-on per seat. Then compare on outcomes: which assistant can answer from your CRM, core banking knowledge base and ticketing with permissions intact? Run a 6-week side-by-side on 3 real use cases and measure answer quality and time saved.

objections.objection: Regulators will not accept AI on customer data.
objections.response: Start with internal knowledge (policies, procedures, product sheets) where no customer PII is needed, keep humans in the loop for anything customer-facing, log every interaction for audit and involve Compliance in the evaluation set. A documented security and PII handling standard plus model risk documentation templates shorten the review.

objections.objection: Our data is a mess — AI will hallucinate.
objections.response: That is why grounding and curation come first: a curated, owned knowledge base with freshness checks, citations on every answer and a 'no answer' behaviour when sources are missing. Data hygiene improves as a side effect.

objections.objection: Per-seat pricing for 2,000 people is too expensive.
objections.response: Segment users: heavy users on the full licence, occasional users on a lighter tier, and agent workloads billed by consumption. Tie the business case to 2-3 measurable processes rather than 'productivity' in general.

proof_points: Fenmoor Credit Union (fictional, 1,800 seats): procedures and product Q&A answered in about 20 seconds instead of a one-day email loop to Operations; 71% weekly active users after 8 weeks
Pellmont Logistics (fictional): dispatch agent grounded on SOPs and the TMS cut onboarding time of new dispatchers from 6 to 3 weeks
Corvane Health (fictional clinic network): 42 internal agents built by business teams in 4 months under one central governance model

competitors: Competitor C — cloud data warehouse sold separately from the hyperscaler
Competitor D — lakehouse platform running on any cloud
Incumbent on-premises warehouse plus BI tool
data_platform.positioning: BigQuery is a serverless, AI-ready data platform: storage and compute separated, no clusters to size, built-in governance and lineage, and Gemini and Vertex AI working directly on governed data — so analytics and AI share one copy of the truth.
strengths: Serverless operations — no warehouses or clusters to size, pause or tune
Native AI on data (SQL functions calling Gemini, vector search, ML) without moving data out
Unified governance: catalog, lineage, policy tags and column-level security
Open formats (Iceberg tables) and multi-engine access to avoid lock-in
Flexible pricing: on-demand for spiky workloads, editions with autoscaling slots for steady ones
landmines: Ask: 'Who sizes, suspends and resumes compute today, and what happens when someone forgets?'
Ask: 'How many copies of your data exist between the lake, the warehouse and the AI team?'
Ask: 'Can you apply column-level masking once and have it hold in every tool?'
Ask: 'What is your cost per query at month-end close, when concurrency peaks?'

objections.response: Use editions with a slot baseline plus autoscaling for steady workloads, set custom quotas and maximum-bytes-billed per user or project, and partition/cluster tables (as in the BigQuery Data Modelling Standards). Most organisations see stable monthly bills within two months.

objections.objection: We are standardising on a lakehouse platform that runs on any cloud.
objections.response: BigQuery reads and writes open table formats, so the choice is not exclusive. Compare total cost including cluster administration, and test AI-on-data scenarios side by side.

objections.objection: Migrating 15 years of warehouse logic is too risky.
objections.response: Use automated SQL translation and a phased migration by subject area with parallel runs and reconciliation reports; start with the domain that has the clearest business owner.

proof_points: Larkspur Outfitters (fictional, 120 stores): daily SKU-store forecasts on BigQuery, stock-outs on top sellers down 18% in the pilot region
City of Port Alder (fictional): 311 service request analytics with SLA tracking built in 8 weeks
Brightwater Distribution (fictional): month-end reporting runtime from 9 hours to 25 minutes after migration

competitors: Incumbent suite — desktop-first productivity suite with email server or cloud mail
Competitor E — team chat platform layered on top of email
workspace_collaboration.positioning: Google Workspace is cloud-native collaboration with security built in and AI included in the workflow: real-time co-editing, one identity, zero-trust access and Gemini in Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Meet and Chat.
strengths: Browser-native real-time collaboration — no file versions emailed around
Security by default: phishing and malware protection, context-aware access, DLP and data regions in eligible editions (verify current edition matrix)
Simple administration for small IT teams
Gemini built into the apps people already use
Proven migration path from Exchange and file shares (a tested cutover-weekend runbook)
landmines: Ask: 'How many people in IT keep the mail servers patched, and what did the last out-of-support server cost you in risk?'
Ask: 'How long does it take to find the latest version of a contract today?'
Ask: 'What would your cyber insurer say about the current mail platform?'

objections.response: Keep desktop Excel for the handful of power users that need it during transition; migrate macro-heavy workbooks selectively to Sheets and Apps Script or BigQuery. Do not let 40 workbooks block 400 users.
Pilot with executive assistants and champions, floor-walkers on day one, and role-based training. A structured hypercare model with floor-walkers resolves most issues in the first 3 days.

objections.objection: We need data to stay in the US/EU.
objections.response: Data regions are available in eligible editions for covered data at rest; confirm the current scope in Google's documentation and design the edition choice accordingly.

proof_points: Tidewell Mutual (fictional insurer, 400 users): planned move off out-of-support mail servers with a 6-month plan and AI claims assistant in the same programme
Pellmont Logistics (fictional): 1,100 users migrated in two waves with zero lost mail and 92% user satisfaction in week 2

competitors: Competitor F — cloud contact-centre platform with built-in bots
Competitor G — conversational AI start-up focused on chatbots
Incumbent on-premises ACD/IVR with scripted menus
contact_center_ai.positioning: Google's Customer Engagement Suite brings generative AI agents to every channel — voice, chat, WhatsApp — grounded on the organisation's own knowledge, with agent assist and conversation insights, and it plugs into the existing contact-centre platform instead of forcing a rip-and-replace.
strengths: Generative agents grounded on enterprise content with guardrails and human hand-off
Agent assist: real-time suggestions and summaries for human agents
Conversation insights across 100% of interactions, not samples
Multilingual speech and text out of the box
Integrates with existing CCaaS and telephony
landmines: Ask: 'What share of contacts could be fully resolved without a human if the bot could read your knowledge base?'
Ask: 'How do you measure quality on 100% of calls today?'
Ask: 'How long does it take to change a bot flow when a policy changes?'

objections.response: Scripted decision-tree bots fail on anything off-script. Generative agents grounded on curated knowledge handle variation, and every conversation has a clear escalation path to a human with the context carried over.

objections.objection: We just renewed our contact-centre platform.
objections.response: No replacement needed: start with agent assist and insights on the current platform, then add virtual agents channel by channel.

proof_points: City of Port Alder (fictional): WhatsApp 311 pilot resolved 41% of information requests without an agent and created tracked service requests for the rest
Corvane Health (fictional): appointment rescheduling bot handled 28,000 conversations a month with 4.5/5 CSAT
